findings.F1: The check failed on Calmar (0.459, with a yearly return of +6.5 %), and the book's deepest falls came on squeeze days, when the coins rose sharply the day after a bounce. The worst book day was −6.3 % on a day the coins rose +12.2 %; that was in w9, whose own deepest fall was −10.6 %. In w14 the book lost −3.2 % and −3.1 % on days the coins rose +11.0 % and +12.5 %. The 40 worst cases had a median next-day rise of +7.1 %, a median position of −0.61 and a median forecast of −14, against −0.24 and −6.4 over all 937 cases.

findings.F3: Agitation is not a short effect of its own; it points the other way. On falling-market days without the signal, the top quartile of the 10-day/60-day swing ratio was followed by a coin rise beyond drift: short gain −1.01 %, t −3.2, 377 days. Agitated non-signal falling days (30-day swing rank above 0.5) gave −0.81 % (227 days). So in agitated downtrends, only the trapped-holder bounce is followed by a fall, which fits the brief's waiting-supply theory.

ideas.idea: In a falling market, the first up day after a run of consecutive down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day. The deeper the run's fall, measured as the coin's return over the run's down days against its usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that fall, and it is larger still the more the coin's swing over the last 10 days exceeds its swing over the last 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades the first relief day in a downtrend hardest when the recent swing has widened, and barely at all when the coin has gone quiet, which avoids the squeezes that made the book's deepest falls.
ideas.name: run-break fade, widening swing

ideas.idea: In a falling market, the first up day after a run of consecutive down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day. The deeper the run's fall against its usual daily swing over the last 30 days, and the deeper the coin's 20-day return, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts relief days mainly inside steep recent slides, where trapped holders are most numerous, and stays small after a mild drift down.
ideas.name: run-break fade, steep slide

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the first up day after a run of consecutive down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day. The deeper the run's fall, measured as the coin's return over the run's down days against its usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps this short for downtrends that are swinging more than usual, and does not take it in calm declines.
ideas.name: agitated falling run-break fade
